## §11 deliverables (by milestone)

### 0.1

engine scaffold, `RevocationEngine`, `Rule`/precedence model with the one-to-one tests, purity gate, BCV, POM assertions; `SymVerifier`, the reference walker and the §9.1 chain generator in `revokt-engine`'s test source set (they move to the published `revokt-testing` in 0.3; the walker fuzzer itself is 0.2, with the walker); TBS/SCT parser (incl. `producerKeyable`, `notBefore`/`notAfter`) with the D7 corpus, the issuer corpus and the §9.2 differential parser oracle (0.1 gate: oracles 1, 2 uber, 3a/3b, 4, properties D1–D3, D5, D6, D8 (gated direction; D8 gap reported)); JSON tree and canonical JSON (§7.1; the content-signature payload builder is 0.2); clubcard port (v3 + v4); the C2SP `index.bin` reader/writer and `GenerationFiles` (`KotlinRevocationEngine.prepare` needs them); the `revokt-engine` jvmMain `Rule → BasicReason` map; oracle CI

### 0.2

a minimal `Revokt` (`build()` and `validate()`, with no `storage` member: the store is `RevoktStorage.inMemory()`; a synchronous `start()` that builds one `CandidateIndex` over `platformTrust.anchors(platformTrust.defaultDelegate())`, loads the seed, runs the in-memory updater on the loader dispatcher and publishes the generation reference, `close()`; the updater syncs in the start task after the seed and then on §5.1's schedule, with the loader's timer and the jitter's random source internal test seams beside `clock` (`RevoktPollTest`), and the first sync can never meet a persisted backoff, the store being fresh at every `build()`; no readiness future, caches, factory lock, per-delegate instances or `state`; start diagnostics returned from `start()` as `List<PolicyDiagnostic>` until `state` exists (`validate()`'s `WARNING`s, then the S `DiagnosticCode`s; the S `WarningCode`s are logged at `WARN`, `SEED_PAST_REJECT_THRESHOLD` too when the loader installs the seed after `start()` returned); the synchronous part runs under one internal lock with no `STARTING` flag (a racing `start()` or `close()` waits for it); in the sole-seed `ENFORCE` configuration a configured seed that opens no archive throws `SEED_UNREADABLE` like an unreadable one; the JVM join is a bounded wait on the start task, measured from the flip; `close()` is the flip, the loader cancelled (its running task interrupted) and awaited without a deadline, the generation reference cleared, then `engine.close()`, with no handshake drain, store lock or identity; the loader thread is `revokt-loader-<build sequence>`, the sequence counting `build()`s in the process from 1; `start()` over an empty or throwing default trust store succeeds, and `evaluator.evaluate` throws `IllegalStateException` until an index exists; `sync()`, `syncAsync()` and `syncBlocking()` are internal and the updater syncs only on its schedule, and so are `SyncResult`, `SyncOutcome`, `SyncFailure`, `RevoktWarning` and `WarningCode`, which have no public consumer before them (the first-consumer rule, §4, #221); `RevoktStorage`, `RevoktLifecycle`, `AnchorSnapshot`, `PathBuilderFallback` and the seam's data types are `@RevoktInternalApi`, and output types have internal builders); candidate index and walker per §5.1, the PKIX fallback (the jvmMain `PkixPathBuilderFallback`, which Android also runs through ojluni, tested on the JVM; the Android instrumented run is 0.3), the §9.2 read fallback in the JVM binding, the walker-only harness, `Evaluator.evaluate` over that one index (decision steps 2–3 and 5–8, walker reason reported directly; `Revokt.evaluate(…, delegate)` is 0.3) with the §9 `Rule` model's [0.2] tests and the §9 API rows; **the §9.1 walker fuzzer is built and runs against the implementation here (P1–P8 gate)** and the walker's adversarial review precedes it; Remote Settings protocol and content-signature verification with x5u path validation (the §9 content-signature fixtures less the three tagged [0.3]); CRLite updater and the updater record over `RevoktStorage.inMemory()` (the §6.5 key layout in memory; durability, `store.version`, pointer flip, crash recovery and the lock are 0.3); seeds with `seed.json`; data artifacts job (GitHub release assets with attestations, not on Maven Central); coverage sanity and rollback; the §9 data-path fixtures (a), (b), (d) and (g) less its Android and OkHttp fetcher halves

### 0.3

moved from 0.2 (#312): the CI-only upki engine and the cross-engine suite (the issuer taken from the corpus chain's presented order, no walk needed), and benchmarks; §6.5 store (`store.version`, `meta.json`, pointer flip, crash recovery, lock); the §9 data-path fixtures (e), (f), (h) and the (g) items deferred from 0.2 (the Android and OkHttp fetcher halves); the §9 content-signature fixtures tagged [0.3] (the restart with the clock behind); caches; per-delegate trust managers and `Revokt.evaluate(…, delegate)`; public `sync()`, `syncAsync()` and `syncBlocking()`, with `SyncResult`, `SyncOutcome`, `SyncFailure`, `RevoktWarning` and `WarningCode`; the `RevoktStorage` factories over its sealed type (§3); lifecycle state machine and readiness future; OkHttp and per-engine Ktor bindings; `OBSERVE` events, `shadowPolicy`, `status()` and `state`, with the §9 `Rule` model's [0.3] tests; Android instrumented suite including the PKIX fallback, the null-host probe and the main-thread wiring probe under `StrictMode.detectDiskReads` on API 26/31/34/36, cold process and after a trust-store change (induced by `am broadcast -a android.security.STORE_CHANGED` as root on AOSP userdebug images, or by installing a user CA through `KeyChain.createInstallIntent()` under UiAutomator on images without root; the mirrored image matrix carries a userdebug variant for this); a consumer fixture built with AGP 8.5.2 that dexes the published artifacts (the Android floor; Appendix A); Baseline Profile and measured `AWAIT_DATA` (JVM default 2 s); WorkManager (`RevoktSyncWorker`, `Revokt.Provider`); system images mirrored into project storage for the emulator matrix; `revokt-testing`, with the output-type test factories (§4); optional `revokt-bc`
